title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Destroying Black Soil Resources

articles.content_en: Article 2 Whoever violates the provisions of the Mineral Resources Law and illegally mines black soil that is a mineral resource, if the conduct meets the requirements of paragraph 1 of Article 343 of the Criminal Law, shall be convicted and punished for the crime of illegal mining.

Article 3 Whoever, in violation of state regulations, discharges, dumps, or disposes of radioactive waste, waste containing infectious disease pathogens, toxic substances, or other harmful substances, thereby causing serious pollution to black soil land, if the conduct meets the requirements of paragraph 1 of Article 338 of the Criminal Law, shall be convicted and punished for the crime of environmental pollution.
Where the act in the preceding paragraph causes the basic functions of 6 mu or more of black soil land that is permanent basic farmland, or 12 mu or more of black soil land other than permanent basic farmland, to be lost or permanently damaged, it shall be deemed as “serious circumstances” under paragraph 1 of Article 338 of the Criminal Law, and the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years, and shall also be fined.
Where the act in paragraph 1 causes the basic functions of 30 mu or more of black soil land that is permanent basic farmland to be lost or permanently damaged, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than seven years, and shall also be fined.

Article 4 Where an act under Article 1, Article 2, or Article 3 of this Interpretation also constitutes the crime of illegal occupation of agricultural land, the crime of illegal mining, or the crime of environmental pollution, the offender shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provisions imposing the heavier punishment.

Article 5 Whoever, knowing that the black soil or the proceeds derived therefrom are proceeds of crime, harbors, transfers, acquires, sells on commission, or disguises or conceals such proceeds by other means, if the conduct meets the requirements of Article 312 of the Criminal Law, shall be properly convicted and sentenced for the crime of disguising or concealing the proceeds of crime and the proceeds derived from such proceeds.
Where a criminal act under the preceding paragraph is committed with prior collusion, the parties shall be dealt with as joint offenders.

Article 7 Whoever organizes others to commit a crime of damaging black soil resources shall be punished in accordance with all the crimes he or she organized and committed.
For persons who are employed to provide labor services for the crime of damaging black soil resources, unless they have previously received criminal punishment for damaging land resources, they shall generally not be considered as committing a crime.

Article 8 Where a unit commits a crime of damaging black soil resources, the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the conviction and sentencing standards provided in this Interpretation, and the unit shall be fined.

Article 9 Where an offender has repeatedly committed crimes of damaging black soil resources that shall be prosecuted according to law, or has repeatedly committed acts of damaging black soil resources within two years without being dealt with, the quantities and amounts shall be cumulatively calculated.

Article 10 When determining whether an act of damaging black soil resources constitutes a crime and when imposing a penalty, the motive and purpose of the act, the degree of damage to black soil resources, whether the ecological environment restoration responsibility has been actively performed, and other circumstances shall be comprehensively considered. The social harmfulness shall be comprehensively evaluated to accurately determine whether the act constitutes a crime and to properly impose a penalty, ensuring proportionality between crime, responsibility, and punishment.

Article 11 Where a person whose relevant act of damaging black soil resources has not been prosecuted, has been acquitted, or has been exempted from criminal punishment, and who shall, according to law, be subject to an administrative penalty, a disciplinary sanction, or other sanction, the relevant authorities shall transfer the case to the competent authority for handling according to law.

Article 12 For specialized factual issues such as the type and area of the black soil land involved in the case, and the volume, quantity, and value of the black soil involved, the determination may be made based on expert evaluation opinions issued by expert evaluation institutions, or recognition opinions issued by competent departments such as agriculture and rural affairs, natural resources, water administration, and ecological environment, or reports issued by price certification bodies, institutions designated or recommended by the relevant competent departments of the State Council, or relevant competent departments of people's governments at or above the prefecture level, in combination with other evidence.

Article 13 For the purposes of this Interpretation, “black soil land” means cultivated land that has a black or dark black humus surface layer, good properties, and high fertility, within the relevant regions of Heilongjiang Province, Jilin Province, Liaoning Province, and the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region as prescribed in paragraph 2 of Article 2 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Black Soil.
Theft excavation, indiscriminate excavation, and illegal sale of black soil from agricultural land within forestland, grassland, wetlands, rivers, lakes, and other areas in the relevant regions specified in the preceding paragraph shall be convicted and sentenced with reference to the provisions of this Interpretation.
Article 14 This Interpretation shall come into force on May 6, 2025.
